record.original_question: Fix a class C of matrices and an integer n, and let C_n be the matrices in C of order at most n. Among the matrices in C_n that are already known to be positive stable, must every such stable matrix satisfy the spectral angle inequality |arg(λ − l(A))| ≤ π/2 − π/n for all eigenvalues λ in σ(A)? The paper asks this for the classes A_{n,k,t}, GKK τ-matrices, GKK matrices, and τ-matrices.

evidence.quote: showed that τ -matrices of order up to 4 satisfy the inequality |arg(λ − l(A))| ≤ π / 2 − π / n ∀λ ∈ σ(A), (2)
3c. For given n, do the stable matrices in class Cn satisfy (2)?

Speciﬁc classes C of interest include i. The class of matrices An,k,t for positive integers n and k, and for t ∈ (0, 1), ii. The class of GKK τ -matrices, iii. The class of GKK matrices, iv. The class of τ -matrices.

artifact.status_search_result: A 2005 work by Holtz–Schneider exhibited unstable GKK τ-matrices (of the form A_{2k+2,k,t}), disproving the broader stability conjectures of Carlson, Engel–Schneider, and Hershkowitz. However, no source located addresses the refined question of whether those members of these classes that are already known to be positive stable must satisfy the spectral angle inequality |arg(λ − l(A))| ≤ π/2 − π/n; this sharper inequality (verified only for τ-matrices of order up to 4) appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Open problems on GKK tau-matrices
status_evidence.snippet: Open problems on GKK tau-matrices, posing several conjectures about stability and spectral inequalities.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is stated as an open problem about stable members of these classes.

status_evidence.title: Not all GKK tau-matrices are stable (Holtz–Schneider)
status_evidence.snippet: A class of unstable GKK τ-matrices A_{2k+2,k,t} is constructed, disproving the stability conjectures.
status_evidence.claim: Stability of the whole class fails, so the refined inequality is asked only for those members already known to be stable.
